title: Knowledge Preservation System
definition: A system that facilitates the creation, storage, and retrieval of permanent, verifiable, and interconnected concepts, resembling a knowledge garden.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a magical garden where you can plant your ideas. Each idea grows into a tree that never forgets what it's learned. And you can link these trees together to help you understand how different ideas are connected.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A knowledge preservation system is a content-addressed digital mycorrhizal intelligence ecosystem. It uses IPLD/DAG-CBOR to store verifiable concepts with unique identifiers. This system allows for deterministic addressing, ensuring same content leads to same CID and understanding.
difficulty_levels.expert: The knowledge preservation system represents a novel application of content-addressed systems in educational knowledge management. It connects to other fields such as cryptography and distributed systems, by leveraging deterministic addressing and DAG-CBOR for data integrity. It also explores ethical knowledge sharing through AGPLv3 with Commons Clause licensing.

extra_fields.insight: The realization that a system can be designed to preserve and grow knowledge, just like a garden, while maintaining data integrity and ethical knowledge sharing.
